name: Never to Return: The Extinct, the Destroyed and the Vanished
description: Mammoths and moas, wonders of the ancient world and a bridge in Bosnia: what we have lost for good, how it was lost and what remains to remember.

checkpoints.name: Before history
checkpoints.note: Woolly mammoths die out and Doggerland sinks under the North Sea. Sumerian fades from speech, Babylon and its Hanging Gardens decay, the Library of Ashurbanipal burns with Nineveh and Rome razes Carthage. The Greek wonders, the Statue of Zeus at Olympia, the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus and the Colossus of Rhodes, are built to be seen and lost.

checkpoints.name: Wonders fall
checkpoints.note: Pompeii lies under ash, the Library of Alexandria fades, and the Lighthouse of Alexandria and the Temple of Artemis fall to earthquake and mobs. People kill off the elephant bird and the moa, while the Buddhas of Bamiyan, carved in the 6th century, stand for another fourteen centuries.

checkpoints.name: The age of the gun and the ship
checkpoints.note: The last aurochs dies in a Polish forest in 1627, sailors kill the dodo and Steller's sea cow and the great auk, and the Globe Theatre burns. The quagga is lost in a zoo in 1883.

checkpoints.name: Twentieth-century losses
checkpoints.note: The passenger pigeon and Carolina parakeet die in captivity, and the last thylacine in 1936. Fire takes the Crystal Palace and the airship Hindenburg, the Amber Room vanishes, and a painting is stolen, and the Berlin Wall, golden toad and Stari Most disappear.

checkpoints.name: The last of their kind
checkpoints.note: The Pyrenean ibex dies out in 2000, the twin towers fall in 2001, the Taliban blow up the Buddhas of Bamiyan, the baiji dolphin is lost, the western black rhinoceros declared extinct, Lonesome George dies and the Antonov An-225 Mriya is destroyed in war.
